While Bavaria (e.g., Oberammergau, Mittenwald) also features façade painting, those towns more often show Bavarian gables and wider streets; the Swiss-style cobbles, iron railings around the fountain, and signage style lean Swiss.

On the right, a building with elaborate stucco frames and mural panels sits immediately at the curb with a climbing vine at the corner and metal bicycle racks below a multi-pane window. These details resemble one of the small squares off the Rathausplatz/Hauptstrasse cluster in Stein am Rhein’s old town, though the exact corner is hard to confirm from this single view. 
Given these cues, I infer the old town of Stein am Rhein, Switzerland, but exact street identification remains uncertain.
